p01.why: Same silhouette; A's head has a closed lipped mouth with two clean fangs, while B's teeth are spiky star-shaped blobs along the jaw.

p02.why: Same armoured silhouette; B's mouth has a lip line with small teeth and fangs, while A's teeth are floating star shapes. B's scale pattern has some black-dot noise, but the mouth outweighs it.

p03.why: Same silhouette; A's abdomen has segment ridges that read as an insect, while B is a smooth featureless blob. Eyes and horn are identical.

p04.why: Silhouette, fangs and eyes are near-identical; A's scales show dithered black-dot noise over the head and neck, while B's cracked-plate skin is clean and reads clearly.

p05.why: Same body, horns and posture; A's head has no mouth at all, while B has a lipped mouth line with a row of small teeth along the jaw.

p06.why: Same horned, striped body; A has a lip line with small teeth plus fangs on the dark muzzle, while B has only a few jagged fangs and no mouth line.

p07.why: Same tiny newt silhouette; A has smooth tapering limbs and a thin lipped mouth, while B's front legs are angular and kinked and the jaw is a chunky block. A's head skin has some speckle noise.

p08.why: Same tusked boar-beast; A has a clear mouth line and smile under the snout, while B has no mouth and a ragged jagged colour edge across the chin and chest.

p09.why: Same long-necked silhouette; A's head has a slim snout with a lip line and teeth, while B has a blocky chin lip and faceted slab skin. A has some dotted scale noise.

p10.why: Same scorpion silhouette; B has banded segments on the tail and legs and a toothed mouth, while A is a smooth tube with no mouth and no joint markings.

p11.why: Same spined serpent; B's mouth is closed with a row of teeth and two fangs in the front view, while A's is a dark gaping hole with star-shaped teeth. B's scales have dot noise.

p12.why: Same small theropod; B has a lipped mouth with a row of rounded teeth and fuller thighs in the front view, while A has star-shaped teeth and straighter stilt-like legs. B has scale noise.

p13.why: Same bear-like beast; A has a lipped mouth line with a row of small teeth and fangs, while B has spiky star-shaped teeth at the front of the jaw and no lip line.

p14.why: Same spotted cat; A has a clean lip line and fuller thighs, while B has a jagged zigzag colour edge around the mouth and straight column legs in the front view.

p15.why: Same gecko-like body; A has a lipped mouth with small teeth and eyelid rims on the eyes, while B's snout has no readable mouth and its eyes are bare spheres. A has some dot noise on the head.

p16.why: Same ant silhouette; B has dark segment rings on the abdomen, thorax and leg joints, which makes it read as an arthropod, while A is a smooth glossy red blob.

p17.why: Same goblin; B has eyelids, brow and nostril bumps, and a lipped mouth with tiny teeth, while A has bare bulging eyes and a ragged jagged dark smear for a mouth.

p18.why: Silhouette and fangs are nearly the same; B's scale skin has heavy black-dot dithering on the head and hood, while A's cracked-plate skin is clean and readable. Low confidence.

p19.why: Same rhino; B has eyelids and a row of small teeth in the mouth, while A has no mouth and plain eyes. A's cracked plates are cleaner, but B's scale skin is noisy.

p20.why: Same spiny dark hound; A has a lip line with clean fangs and red eyes with lid rims, while B has a row of star-shaped teeth and bare bulb eyes.
